clue.text: Single out the Queen with extremes of admiration? He might

definitions.text: Single out the Queen with extremes of admiration? He might

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the word before it are put out of their usual order

parts.note: HM stands for Her Majesty, a common way to refer to the Queen

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here taken from admiration

explanation.surface: A loyal subject picks out the monarch for special admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SINGLE into ENGLIS; HM and A...N (first and last letters of 'admiration') follow. The whole clue describes a patriot who would do just that.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriotic native of England is the sort of person who might single out the monarch for admiration.

indicators.note: a guillotined body loses its head, so the word for aristocrats loses its first letter

parts.note: toffs is British slang for upper-class people, aristocrats

explanation.surface: A grim scene from the French Revolution, with nobles going under the blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guillotined' cuts the head off TOFFS (British slang for posh people), leaving the slang verb meaning kills.
explanation.definitionFit: To 'off' someone is slang for killing them, so the third-person form matches executes.

indicators.note: overturning means the word for unchanged is turned the other way round

parts.note: something unchanged stays the same

explanation.surface: A school stubbornly reverses its decision to keep its plans as they were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturning' reverses SAME to EMAS, which follows SCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Schemas are outlines or frameworks, a synonym for plans or diagrams.

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
a pint is a measure of liquid

indicators.note: the inception of a word is its beginning, so take the first letter of open

explanation.surface: Volunteers measure the start of a scheme offering open access to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's volunteer reserve; a pint is a measure; 'inception of' gives the first letter of 'open'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap into a resource is to gain access to it and draw on it.

indicators.note: among means the comedian's first name goes inside the rearranged letters
excited suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: the possessive Derby's gives the letters of Derby plus S
Stan Laurel was half of the comedy double act Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: A famous comedian is spotted in the crowd at an exciting Derby, the horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges DERBYS into BYDERS; 'among' puts STAN (Stan Laurel) inside it. The Derby is England's most famous horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Bystanders are onlookers who watch an event without taking part.

clue.text: Appearance of umpire regularly gets bit of needle

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of umpire, here the second, fourth and sixth
a bit of the word needle is its first letter

explanation.surface: An umpire keeps getting jabbed by a sharp object during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'umpire', MIE; 'bit of' adds the first letter of 'needle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing or look, a literary word for appearance or demeanour.

parts.note: the letters are a lamp spelt backwards, so a source of light turned the wrong way

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a picture: PMAL is LAMP written backwards, a light that is reversing. It names the lamp on a car that comes on when it backs up.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversing light is the white lamp at a car's rear that shines when backing.

clue.text: "To Elton … a trout-farm," as heard by him?

indicators.note: as heard means the words are said out loud and the sound is what goes in the grid

parts.note: the comedian Ben Elton is addressed by first name, and a trout-farm is a fishery: a bequest reading Ben, a fishery

explanation.surface: A line from a will leaves a fish farm to the comedian Ben Elton.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a bequest in a will, 'To Elton' is 'Ben', and spoken quickly 'Ben, a fishery' sounds like the answer. The definition 'him' is the person receiving it.
explanation.definitionFit: The person named in a will who receives a bequest is the heir or recipient, so 'him' is the legatee.

clue.text: Conductor's given leave to make hardly a change

definitions.text: Conductor's given leave to make hardly a change

parts.words: Conductor's given leave to make hardly a change
parts.note: a bus conductor's time off, if spent riding buses, would be no real break from work

explanation.surface: A bus conductor is granted time off, but it barely feels any different from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests an orchestra but means the ticket collector on a bus; the phrase describes free time spent doing what you do at work.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a holiday spent doing the same thing as one's usual job, hence hardly a change.

clue.text: Borderers from Irvine pocket church silver in hard times

indicators.note: to pocket is to take inside, so the outer letters enclose the church and silver
the borderers of a word are its first and last letters, taken from Irvine

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Raiders from the Scottish town of Irvine steal church silver during hard years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borderers from' takes I...E, the first and last letters of 'Irvine'; 'pocket' places CE (Church of England) and AG (silver) between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacial period was a literal frozen era, and figuratively a bleak spell, so hard times fits doubly.

clue.text: Difficulty gaining purchase involves ceaseless strain

indicators.note: involves is read as entangling or twisting together the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Getting a grip on a climb requires relentless effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' rearranges CEASELESS STRAIN. 'purchase' looks like grip, but means buying.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the reluctance of customers to buy, which makes it hard for a seller to secure a purchase.

clue.text: When Southampton player, Shearer's back in as striker

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

indicators.note: in means the reversed name goes inside the word for the Southampton player

parts.note: Southampton football club are nicknamed the Saints

indicators.note: back means the short name is read from end to start

parts.note: Alan Shearer, the England footballer, shortened to Al

explanation.surface: Alan Shearer returns to Southampton, his first club, and plays as their striker.
explanation.walkthrough: AL (short for Alan Shearer) read back is LA, which goes 'in' SAINT (a Southampton player) after AS. 'striker' suggests a footballer, but means an attacker.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is someone who attacks or strikes another person.

definitions.meaning: a ship built to cut through frozen seas
a remark or game that eases tension at the start of a gathering

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a ship that clears frozen channels; the other is an opening activity that relaxes strangers socially.

parts.note: barely means without clothes, so these are paintings or sculptures of unclothed figures

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' seems to mean 'scarcely', but read as 'in the bare' it describes paintings of unclothed figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings and sculptures of unclothed models are a classic genre of art.

clue.text: Dick tears up first bits of important treatise editor's downcast

parts.note: dick is slang for a detective, and DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: tears as a verb means rips

indicators.note: the first bits of the two words are their opening letters

parts.note: ED is a standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A detective angrily rips up the opening pages of an important paper, and its editor is crestfallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RIPS to SPIR in this down clue; 'first bits of' takes I and T from 'important treatise'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispirited means having lost heart, a synonym of dejected or low.

clue.text: Reckoning on embracing Essex island's lucrative period …

indicators.note: embracing means the first pair of words wraps around the island's name

parts.note: a sum is a reckoning or calculation
taken as written
Mersea is an island off the coast of Essex, with the possessive adding S

explanation.surface: Counting on a small Essex island for a profitable stretch of tourist trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts MERSEAS between SUM and ON. Mersea Island lies off the Essex coast in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiday resorts make most of their money in the warm months when tourists arrive.

parts.note: to hog something is to keep it selfishly for oneself
wee is Scottish for little
D is a standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A greedy parent takes the small daughter's vegetable from her plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because hogweed is also called cow parsnip.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogweed belongs to the carrot family and is commonly known as cow parsnip.

parts.note: Glow-worm is the setter, so the setter refers to themself as me
hands are workers, men
a door pushed to is closed

explanation.surface: The setter keeps their hands shut tight as a keepsake.
explanation.walkthrough: Glow-worm is the setter's pseudonym; 'to' as in 'push the door to' means closed.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a souvenir kept as a reminder, an object of remembrance.

parts.note: to own up is to admit, so own means admit
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A landlady has to let a royal visitor in.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the previous clue for the surface only. ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlady is the proprietor of a lodging house, holding the property she lets.

clue.text: Bit too much for some cricket ball?

parts.note: overs are the sets of six deliveries that make up a cricket innings
pill is slang for a ball in sport

explanation.surface: A question of whether a cricket ball has been bowled too often.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket; 'pill' is old slang for a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspill is an excess that spills beyond a limit, more than there is room for.

clue.text: Rigid lawn tennis regulation produces very different sport

indicators.note: regulation suggests putting letters into a new order by rule
very different says the letters end up in quite another arrangement

explanation.surface: Strict rules at a tennis club give rise to an altogether different game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulation' and 'very different' both rearrange RIGID LAWN TENNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian wrestling is a contest of strength, such as arm wrestling, and so a sport.

definitions.meaning: to do someone is slang for swindling them

explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is to swindle them; female deer and rabbits are also so named.

indicators.note: sounding means the word for educated is said out loud

parts.note: someone educated has been taught

explanation.surface: Someone sounds well schooled but is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pronunciation the word for educated sounds just like the legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: A tort is a civil wrong in law, such as negligence or trespass.

clue.text: Hole in crippled jet creates means of escape

indicators.note: in means the hole goes inside the rearranged letters
crippled says the letters of the jet are smashed out of order

parts.note: O is shaped like a hole

explanation.surface: A damaged jet aircraft has a hole that gives the pilot a way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crippled' rearranges JET CREATES; 'in' places O (a hole) among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejector seat fires a pilot out of a stricken aircraft, an escape mechanism.
